summary: The one finding (medium) was verified at its evidence and is confirmed, with a narrowed and made-definite fix. The extraction's sourceIssues and the errata file both carry PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/E1 and /E2, and the two records disagree. The errata review (e3c377e9, 2026-09-23 12:34 UTC) narrowed E1 to affect 'the proof'. It also changed E2's correction to m ≥ 2, in Demarche's convention where Q_4 ≅ C_4. The paper review (5069b0bd, 18:28 UTC) then confirmed the extraction's older versions: 'a stated result', and m ≥ 3. I reproduced scripts/errata.py collect() read-only at f63511f2, and it returns four HW20 entries: E1 twice with different 'affects', and E2 twice with different corrections. I re-derived both mistakes from the author manuscript (SHA-256 matches), arXiv v2, Demarche's author manuscript and Wit18. E1: §4 fixes a rationally connected generic fibre. Remarque 4.5 applies Théorème 4.2(i) to a fibration whose geometric generic fibre is birational to V × torus, so that fibre is rationally connected iff X is. Wit18 Remark 3.9 asserts the implication without rational connectedness, and nothing shows that it fails. So 'the proof' is the right reach, and rational connectedness of X is a sufficient repair, not the correction. E2: Demarche §8 defines Q_(2^n) for n ≥ 2, and at m = 2 the presentation gives C_4, for which SL_n/C_4 is rational; so m ≥ 2 is right. Items 75, 104 and 105 are true as stated, as restrictions, which is why the severity is medium, not high. Corrections to the red team's fix: (1) sourceIssues becomes [] next to a sourceIssueReferences entry, rather than being deleted, following PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18. (2) Items 104 and 105 take m ≥ 2; the red team offered m ≥ 2 or m ≥ 3. (3) Item 75's statement is kept; only its locator and note change. (4) The matching text of the extraction's .md is in scope. (5) The fixer does not rewrite REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md: this verdict supersedes its E1/E2 verdicts. (6) The fixer does not run scripts/errata.py and does not edit REGISTER.md or data/source-issues.json, since the intake regenerates them after the merge.

sources.citation: Harpaz–Wittenberg, Zéro-cycles sur les espaces homogènes et problème de Galois inverse, author manuscript (26 February 2018, revised 23 September 2019), the version recorded by the extraction and the red team; hash matches. Read the quaternion paragraph of the introduction (p. 4), §3 through Proposition 3.3 and Remarque 3.4 (pp. 12–15) and §4 through Remarque 4.5 (pp. 15–17). The version of record is J. Amer. Math. Soc. 33 (2020), no. 3, 775–805, doi 10.1090/jams/943; not collated, as for the extraction and both reviews. The finding concerns how the atlas records the mistakes, not the published wording.
arXiv 1802.09605v2; hash matches the errata review's record.

Demarche, author manuscript of Dem10: Corollaire 4.5 and Remarque 4.6 (p. 12), and §8 (p. 26): 'si n ≥ 2, on note Q_(2^n) le groupe des quaternions d'ordre 2^n', with X_n = SL_m/Q_(2^n) rational for n = 2, 3.

Wittenberg (Wit18), Theorem 3.7, Corollary 3.8 and Remark 3.9 (pp. 21–22). Remark 3.9 asserts the universal-torsor implication for X as in Theorem 3.7 only: k̄[X]^× = k̄^× and Pic(X_k̄) free of finite rank, with no rational connectedness.

findings.reason: Checked at every locator at f63511f2. None of the files involved has changed since the red team's input revision 6bfc27fb: the extraction, errata file, paper review, PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 and scripts/errata.py, check_paper.py and check_errata.py. (a) The double record. PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.result.json sourceIssues has E1 (gap, affects 'a stated result', correction 'Add the hypothesis that X is rationally connected') and E2 (correction 'm ≥ 3'), both reviewed by REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20. errata/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.json has the same ids: E1 affects 'the proof', and the correction reads 'Adding rational connectedness of X is a sufficient restricted repair, not a demonstrated necessary hypothesis …'. E2's correction there is 'Use m ≥ 2 if following the convention in the cited Demarche author manuscript, which includes Q_4≅C_4'. Both carry REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20 verdicts, and the older versions are kept in assessmentHistory as superseded. Commit times: e3c377e9 (errata review) 2026-09-23 12:34:54 UTC, 5069b0bd (paper review) 18:28:01 UTC. REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md says 'both sourceIssues confirmed' and restates E1 as '(gap, a stated result)' and E2 as m ≥ 3. A read-only call of scripts/errata.py collect() returns four HW20 entries, each 'confirmed': E1 from the result file ('a stated result') and from the errata file ('the proof'), and E2 from each. REGISTER.md lines 8054–8057 print all four. (b) The mathematics, re-derived. E1: §4 (p. 15) fixes 'un morphisme dominant f : X → P^n_k dont la fibre générique est rationnellement connexe', and Théorème 4.1's hypotheses 'sont ici satisfaites en vertu de [GHS03]'. In Remarque 4.5 (p. 17) the fibres of π′ are universal torsors of V, and over k̄ a torsor under a split torus is Zariski-locally trivial. So the geometric generic fibre is birational to V × torus, which is rationally connected iff X is. X need not be rationally connected under the remark's hypotheses: a K3 surface has torsion-free Pic. So the citation of Théorème 4.2(i) is out of scope. But Proposition 3.3(i) (p. 14) gives the geometric section with no rational-connectedness hypothesis, Wit18 Remark 3.9 asserts the implication in full generality, and nothing shows that the implication fails. Under PROTOCOL §18 that is a gap in the proof, not in a stated result, so the errata review's narrowing is right. Rational connectedness of X is a sufficient repair: with it, the §4 setting holds, the fibres over codimension-1 points of Q are split because π is smooth, and CTS87 gives Br₁(Z) = Br₀(Z). So item 75's restricted statement is true. E2: page 4 prints 'Q_(2^m) … pour un entier m ≥ 1'. Demarche's §8 (p. 26 of the author copy) defines Q_(2^n) for n ≥ 2. At m = 2 the relations give x = y² and y⁴ = 1, so Q_4 ≅ C_4, and Demarche notes that SL_m/Q_(2^n) is rational for n = 2, 3. So the corrected statement holds for m ≥ 2. The known cases 'm ≤ 4' in HW's text do not force m ≥ 3. Items 104 and 105 as written (m ≥ 3) are true but drop the source's endpoint, and item 104's note calls m ≥ 3 'the standard range' and speaks of 'nonexistent standard groups'. (c) sourceVersions: scripts/check_paper.py applies only source_issues.check_issues, not check_errata.versions_checked (check_errata.py:35–38). That is why the extraction passes ('ok', rerun) with an E1 affecting 'a stated result' and no sourceVersions. The problem disappears once E1 leaves the extraction. (d) Adversarial checks on the red team. Doubled ids are systemic: collect() finds 676 ids recorded in two files, across 38 owners, most with the same content. The mere duplication is therefore a register-tooling matter, and it goes in a maintainer note. What is specific to HW20, and confirmed, is that the two records conflict and that the extraction's items follow the superseded versions. Medium is right: the public register shows contradictory verdicts, but no item states anything false, so nothing built changes. Corrections to the red team's fix: it offered 'm ≥ 2 or m ≥ 3', and m ≥ 2 is chosen; it asked for REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md to be rewritten and the register regenerated, and both are dropped as outside a fixer's files (the intake's ALLOWED paths exclude data/ and research/errata/, and the intake regenerates both after merge). Authorised fix, in research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.result.json and the matching text of PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md only: (1) Set sourceIssues to [] (keep the key) and add sourceIssueReferences: [{'file': 'research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.json', 'ids': ['PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/E1', 'PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20/E2'], 'note': 'Recorded and reviewed there (REV-ERRATA-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20); kept in one place to avoid duplicate register entries. E1 affects the proof; E2 uses m ≥ 2 with Q_4 ≅ C_4.'}], as PAPER-TSIMERMAN-18 does. (2) Item 75: keep the statement, status (missing) and route. Its locator becomes 'Remark 4.5 p.17, restricted to rationally connected X, a sufficient repair (E1)'. Replace the note's opening ('Corrected statement … The printed remark omits that X is rationally connected.') with: the printed remark cites Theorem 4.2(i) outside its rationally connected setting (E1, a gap in the proof); rational connectedness of X is a sufficient repair, under which the argument goes through as the note then explains; the printed generality, as asserted in Wit18 Remark 3.9, would need a section-based variant of Theorem 4.2(i) using the geometric section of Proposition 3.3(i), which is neither stated nor proved here and remains open (the former G1). Keep the Sko90 sentence. (3) Items 104 and 105: 'm≥3' becomes 'm≥2' in both statements. Item 104's note ends: 'The source introduction writes m≥1; following Demarche's convention (Dem10 author version §8), Q_(2^m) is defined for m≥2, with Q_4 ≅ C_4 the cyclic case and m≥3 the non-abelian groups (E2).' Delete 'use the standard generalized-quaternion range m≥3 … nonexistent standard groups'. Item 105's note cites E2 in the same way. (4) The summary sentence 'two findings are recorded (E1 on Remark 4.5, E2 a misprint in the quaternion range)' becomes: the two mistakes are recorded in the errata file (E1 a gap in the proof of Remark 4.5; E2 the quaternion range, m ≥ 2). (5) In the .md: in the 'Remark 4.5 … now E1' paragraph, 'Item 75 now states this corrected version' becomes 'Item 75 states this restricted version, a sufficient repair; the printed generality remains open'. The 'E2 (misprint), p. 4' paragraph and the 'standard generalized-quaternion range is m≥3' sentence of the Grunwald paragraph say m ≥ 2 as in (3). The 'Mistakes found (sourceIssues)' section is replaced by a pointer to the errata file with the two current verdicts. The appended 'Review (REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20 …)' section is a record of that review and stays. Maintainer notes, not fixer edits: this verdict supersedes the E1/E2 verdicts in REV-PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-20.md, which the fixer does not rewrite. After the merge the intake's scripts/errata.py run lists each HW20 mistake once. errata.py lists every id that appears in both an extraction and an errata file twice (676 ids, 38 owners), and check_paper.py does not run the sourceVersions check. Both are tooling matters for the maintainer.
